name: Designing the Programme — Win the NorthGrid Mandate at Pennine Executive Learning
description: A four-round, advanced executive-education simulation set inside Pennine Executive Learning, the open-and-custom exec-ed unit of a research-intensive UK business school in Manchester (£14.2m turnover, 32% blended margin, 70% of custom revenue from six anchor clients). On 8 June 2026 a £1.8m anchor-client RFP lands with a four-week clock: NorthGrid Utilities, a £6bn regulated energy group and Pennine's second-largest custom client, wants 120 senior leaders 'ready to run a decarbonised, digitised business within 12 months', cohort 1 live in 10 weeks, against two rival bidders. The brief is ambitious, vague and contested — the CHRO sponsor wants behaviour change, the divisional MDs want technical reskilling, HR wants a reusable asset — and the obvious faculty-heavy bespoke design costs £2.6m against a £1.8m budget (£15k per head), an £0.8m gap the team must close through format and delivery choices, not by cutting the outcome. Playing the design team, you (1) diagnose the true learning need and the decision-economic buyer, converting a vague aspiration into measurable, outcome-linked objectives and segmenting the 120 leaders; (2) choose open vs custom vs hybrid architecture, trading client-needs fit against cost and time-to-launch under the fixed envelope; (3) configure the blended delivery-mode mix and allocate the 3 of 5 available senior strategy faculty to the highest-leverage moments only — without cannibalising £0.6m of open revenue — while confirming ≥30% margin, a 10-week launch and Kirkpatrick L3/L4 impact measurement; and (4) pitch to the CHRO and procurement, defending scope and price against more-days and discount demands and offering a phased cohort-1 proof as the win-protecting move. The math rewards client-first, constraint-aware solution architecture and punishes the five classic errors — designing before diagnosing, bespoke-by-default, cheap-by-default, faculty over-allocation, and giving away margin — measured on Client Fit, Contribution Margin %, Launch Readiness and Win Probability.

8 June 2026 · Pennine Executive Learning · NorthGrid RFP — £1.8m, 120 leaders, 4-week clock

Designing the Programme

A £1.8m anchor-client RFP has landed with two rivals bidding. NorthGrid wants 120 senior leaders ready to run a decarbonised business in 12 months, cohort 1 live in 10 weeks. The obvious bespoke design costs £2.6m. Architect a solution that fits the client, closes the £0.8m gap, and holds the 30% margin floor — or lose the mandate and 24% of the custom pipeline.

Round 1 — Diagnose the learning need, not the agenda

Your Decisions This Round

Objectives tied to business outcomes, not topics: 50
Custom spine share (rest is modular open): 50%
~40–60% custom keeps the relevant content NorthGrid-specific while open modules cover finance and digital fundamentals cheaply.
In-person intensives — high impact, high cost, faculty-led
Virtual-live sessions — moderate cost, scalable
Asynchronous digital modules — low cost, scalable
Coaching + on-the-job application projects — drives L3/L4 impact
Total per-learner days: 6.5 (target 6–10)
Facilitator (Managing Director & NorthGrid CHRO in the room)
This is a commercial decision as much as a pedagogical one. Before you design a single module, tell me what NorthGrid's 120 leaders will do differently on Monday morning and who judges whether it worked. The bespoke design costs £2.6m against an £1.8m budget — you close that gap with format and delivery choices, not by cutting the outcome. And I will not approve a bid below 30% margin. Diagnose first, architect the format, configure delivery and faculty under the cap, then defend the margin in the room.
